In [[mathematics]], in the realm of [[group theory]], a '''normal automorphism''' of a group is an [[group automorphism|automorphism]] that takes every [[normal subgroup]] bijectively to itself.<ref name="MO2010">
{{cite journal
|title = Normal automorphisms of relatively hyperbolic groups 
|last1= Minasyan
|first1 = A. 
|last2= Osin
|first2= D.
|journal = [[Trans. Amer. Math. Soc.]]
|volume = 362 (2010), 6079-6103
|doi = 10.1090/S0002-9947-2010-05067-6
|mr = 2661509
|arxiv = 0809.2408
}}</ref> As a result, it gives a corresponding automorphism for every [[quotient group]].

All [[family automorphism]]s are normal, and particularly, all [[class automorphism]]s and [[power automorphism]]s are. As well, all [[inner automorphism]]s are normal (but not vice versa),<ref name="MO2010"/> and more generally, any automorphism defined by an ''[[algebraic formula]]'' is normal.
